_doc: One title's cabinet. `make -C introlab cabinet TITLE=altbeast` reads this file and writes
everything under introlab/art/altbeast/ (gitignored: it is derived from Sega artwork).
Paths are relative to the repository root; a path missing from a worktree is looked up
in the main checkout, because the artwork is untracked and lives only there.
The tools expect the model, after `rotate_deg`, to stand with +Z up and its front on +X.
title: altbeast

lift.why: bezel and screen decal, coplanar with a plain face
marquee decal, coplanar with a plain face

banner.why: the marquee, shown flat beside the cabinet; a region that replaces this whole face replaces the banner too

font.why: the game's own 8x8 text tiles, in ASCII order from space; plane 0 is the face, plane 1 its shadow

room.why: the room's sounds: numbers of the captured effects under art/<title>/room (tools/gen_room.py). Mike's picks by ear, 2026-11-14; they are to sit under the crowd murmur, not over it. murmur = the crowd bed's level on FM channels 1-2 (a TL: smaller is louder, 0 = none). OFF: the first recipe sounded like an engine (Mike); the next is chosen by ear from rendered previews before it is built

backdrops._doc: the room's back wall; `make cabinet BACKDROP=<name>` picks another. At most 18 colours.

moon.why: rows dropped only where every shape is a plain vertical, so nothing but column height changes

beasts.why: only the beasts the centurion turns into; `sink` moves a figure down (negative: up, into the sky)

replace.why: the model's own marquee artwork (1600x502), taken straight from the file: the bake of it is soft and cropped

JP marquee (1600x502, same shape as the US one): 獣王記 logo in the instruction card's own pale blue and navy, supplied by Mike, on the red of the JP arcade instruction card (segaretro AlteredBeast_System16_JP_InstructionCard.jpg)
